unresolved.question: Is the mark under the first ת a qamats (שְׁתָתוֹ) or a sheva, and is there a dagesh in that ת (שְׁתְּתוֹ)? The final vav shows a holam dot, which matches the current text.
Is the dot on the vav at mid-height on its left (shuruq) or at the top (holam, שְׁעוֹן)?
Is the vowel under ש a patah bar or a hiriq dot, and does the yod carry a dagesh like the rhyming ‑יָּה words (לִשְׁעִיָּה / לְשַׁעְיָּה)?
Under the ב of רבעה, is it a qamats or a qubuts, and is there a dagesh? Is there a dagesh in the yod of היום? Both earlier independent reads had הַיּוֹם.
Is the mark under ח a hataf-patah or a plain sheva, and does the ת carry a dagesh (לְקַחְתָּהּ)? The mappiq in the final ה is visible.
Is the second letter a dalet with a sharp corner, like the ד in the next word מִזֵּד, or a rounded resh (פְּרוּתָהּ)? Do not settle this from meaning.
Is there a dagesh inside the ב? I cannot see one at this size.
Is the first letter of each word a ב with a base stroke or a rounded כ? At this size both look close to the כ of כַּעֲקֶרֶת.

Is the vowel under נ a sheva (נְכָרָה, with qamats under כ and ר) or a hiriq? Is there a dagesh in כ? The marks look like a sheva under נ and a qamats under each of כ and ר, which differs from the current נִכְרָה.
Under ת and the third letter, is it a segol (three dots) or a tsere (two)? Is the third letter ב or כ (the s126–133 audit queried בְּתֹכֶל)?
Is there a dagesh dot in the ת? The blind and image-only reads had תַּ; the current text has no dagesh.
